question_text:
X's father raised him with the explicit goal of creating a genius intellect. Today X is best known for his essay Y. Y was originally attributed to just him, but scholars now agree that it was coauthored with his wife Harriet Taylor. Y deals with the relationship between the individual and the state. It argues that the only justified reason for a society to exercise power over an individual against their will is to prevent direct harm to others. Vikram Seth's poem Diwali contains this verse:

The undigested Hobbes
The ____ who later ground
(Through talk of _______)
The Raj out of the land

The first blank is X's last name and the second blank is the bulk of Y.

ID X (5) and Y (5).

The name X means "the victorious one." In his book 499 CE book, AryabhaTa uses the line of longitude running through X as the prime meridian, and calculates that when the sun rises in X, it is midnight in rOmaka (presumably Rome). Time itself is still worshipped in this city. X was the capital of one of the 16 mahAjanapadas of India. It remained the preeminent city of the _____ plateau controlling important trade routes until early modern times, serving as the capital of the _____ subah under the Mughals. Both blanks are the same. ID X.

It was formed by bringing together three separate standards of countries that fought one another bitterly during the Middle Ages. X smashes together the St. ______'s Cross, the St. _______'s Saltire, and the St. _______'s Saltire. What is it?
answer_text: Union Jack, the flag of the United Kingdom

question_text: Jiang Qing (Mao Zedong's last wife) and her close associates Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan, and Wang Hongwen are collectively known to history by a famous nickname. They rose to prominence during the Cultural Revolution in the mid-1960s. After the ignominious end of that revolution, they were convicted of treasonous crimes and sentenced to long prison terms. The picture shows a poster vilifying the group. What is the group's nickname that has spread to other fields as well? For example: An English post-punk band: their debut album Entertainment! was rated by Rolling Stone as the fifth greatest punk album of all time; The collective name for the authors of the software engineering book Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software; A popular Asian card game from Hong Kong

X told ESPN Cricinfo in 2017 that he had three posters on his bedroom wall: Karl Marx, the goddess Lakshmi, and the cricketer M.L. Jaisimha. He talked fondly of playing as an off spinner on a team captained by Ranji cricketer R.A. Swaroop and the lessons he learned there that helped him excel in his future career. He added: "I went to the United States right when Sachin Tendulkar started to play for India so I look at it and say, wow, I missed the entire Sachin era of Indian cricket." ID X.
This is a family tree. It shows the earliest and latest dates when each branch of the tree diverged from its closest neighbors. What family does this tree represent?

Samuel Cooper painted this portrait of X in 1656 CE. Cooper asked X how he wanted the portrait to look. X told Cooper to paint everything he saw using the three-word phrase Y. This contrasted with how most rulers of the time were painted like flawless Roman statues. X's biggest achievement was the only overthrow of monarchy in English history. He died of malaria, but when monarchy was restored, royalists dug up his body from Westminster Abbey, hung it in chains, and beheaded it. The phrase Y that X coined now means "to show something exactly as it is, including its unpleasant or unattractive aspects." ID X (5) and Y (5).

Padma Bhushan Kesarbai Kerkar was a Hindustani classical vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharAna. She is one of the most influential classical singers of the 20th century. Rabindranath Tagore gave her the title "surashrI" meaning "master of musical notes." She enjoys a unique distinction amongst Indian classical musicians. Her out-of-this-world rendition of jAt kahAn hO in Raga Bhairavi brought her this distinction. What distinction?
answer_text: She is the only Indian musician whose work is featured on the Voyager Golden Record.

question_text: The golden age in the history of this city was between the 14th and 16th centuries CE, when it was a key hub in the trans-Saharan trade network. Over the centuries, it changed hands from the Mali Empire to the Tuaregs to the Songhai Empire to the Moroccans to the French. In its heyday it attracted visitors like Ibn Battuta and Leo Africanus and had a university with scholars in Islamic law, mathematics, and astronomy. Salt used to fetch its weight in gold in this city known for its riches. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Name this remote city located on a bend of the river Niger where it runs north through the Sahara before turning south towards Nigeria.

The term X originates from Greek where it means "housekeeping" and "administration," derived from "oῖκος" meaning "house." In the Roman Empire, X was an administrative unit at the intermediate level of government. Each X aggregated several provinces, and several neighboring Xs together formed a praetorian prefecture. An official called vicarius was appointed to oversee each X. The smallest such X was Britannia, composed of four provinces. We now know X primarily in a church context. ID X.

X was an engineer by training. As a young man, he joined a progressive-utopian literary society that discussed banned books. In 1849 he was convicted of the crime of treason and sentenced to death. As X was lined up to be shot by a firing squad, he had a hard time figuring out what was going on because of his acute myopia. The king had commuted his sentence at the last minute and gave him the punishment of prison instead. He developed epilepsy in prison and was released due to poor health. X then went on to write his best-known novels. He was a compulsive gambler and died in penury despite earning large sums for his books. ID X.

In 1980, the Polish-language poet Czesław Miłosz received an important professional recognition. He seized the moment to ask his employer X for a reserved parking spot. His employer granted the request, and that began a tradition at X. X now has around 10 dedicated parking spots for people who have achieved this recognition. ID X (7) and the recognition (3) that makes you eligible for a reserved parking spot at X.
answer_text: X=University of California, Berkeley; recognition=being a Nobel Laureate (Nobel Prize)

question_text: When public-sector employee unions in India negotiate wages with various governments, one of the most important items on the table is called DA. The concept was introduced after the end of World War II. Back then, the phenomenon that DA addresses did not yet have its current popular name. What does DA stand for (3), and what phenomenon does it seek to address (7)?
answer_text: DA=Dearness Allowance; phenomenon=cost of living adjustments for inflation

question_text: 42nd Street is a 1980 Broadway production that won Tony Awards for Best Musical and Best Choreography. The plot involves small-town chorus girl Peggy Sawyer landing a spot in the ensemble of a massive Broadway production. She must unexpectedly step into the lead role when the show's star breaks her ankle. Peggy delivers a show-stopping performance and becomes a star. Now, to the interesting part that happened at the London production of the show in 1987: X was a teenage chorus member when the actress playing Peggy Sawyer was on vacation and her understudy fell ill. X filled in as Peggy and a producer in the audience was impressed with her performance and cast her permanently in the role soon after. She won the Best Supporting Actress Oscar in the movie adaptation of another stage musical over a decade later. ID X.

Charition Mime is a Greek theater play found in a 2nd century CE papyrus that was discovered in Egypt. It is the only known ancient Greek play that is set in India. In this farcical play, Charition (Χαριτίων) is a Greek woman held captive by an Indian king at a temple to a moon goddess. Her brother leads a group across the sea to rescue her. One fascinating feature of this play is dialog in an unknown language. These lines are intended as amusing gibberish for the Greek audience. The leading theory is that these lines are in an ancient form of either X or Y, both spoken now in the same state. ID either X or Y for the full 10 points. Either answer is enough to close the question.

Confederados are an ethno-religio-cultural group in Brazil. They are the descendants of 20,000 people from X who migrated to Brazil when Emperor Dom Pedro II offered cheap land and the legality of Y as incentives, hoping to establish a cotton industry in Brazil. When Y was outlawed in Brazil two decades later, many immigrants went back to X, but some remained and their descendants now number around 260,000 people. The photo shows their annual cultural festival called Festa Confederada. ID X (5) and Y (5).
answer_text: X=United States of America (the south in particular); Y=Slavery

question_text: The world's third-largest island (excluding continents) was known to ancient Indians as suvarNabhUmi ("land of gold") and as karpUradvIpa ("camphor island"). The island is home to some of the world's oldest rainforests. The local name is Kalimantan, but the answer to this question is a Portuguese corruption of the name of a kingdom that once ruled the whole island. In colonial times, part of the island was ruled by three generations of "White Rajahs" of British ancestry. It is the only island in the modern world ruled by three countries: ______, Indonesia, and Malaysia. Name the island.

In a widely discussed 2022 technical report, AI researcher and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun argued that Large Language Models (LLMs) will never achieve Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) because they lack an internalized, structured representation of how things work, including physical causality, object permanence, and the consequences of actions. He claimed that AI systems must learn these primarily from video and sensory experience rather than from text, putting him in direct and public conflict with researchers who believed simply scaling up LLMs was the path to AGI. He is now working to build an alternative to LLMs. What is he building?
